title: Hybrid Metering: Unified Usage Mapping & Billing Exposure for Hosted + Dedicated Entitlements
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: Define and implement a single mapping layer and billing exposure that correctly attributes usage and cost for mixed-mode customers that use Redwood Hosted API and Redwood Dedicated capacity. Current gap: invoices and console breakdowns treat hosted and dedicated usage separately and use different metering semantics (token-based hosted vs. compute-credit-based dedicated), causing confusing invoices and reconciliation work for customers that split traffic across modes. Goal: provide a clear, explainable per-caller/per-route billing breakdown and one canonical ledger view that supports committed capacity, per-model overrides, and negotiated smoothing windows for enterprise customers.
background: We have increasing customers using hybrid deployments (hosted for burst/experiments, dedicated for steady traffic). Finance and Support report frequent billing questions where per-token hosted meters don't align with dedicated compute-credit consumption. Sales asks for a clear contract view and invoice sections showing how burst spillover and negotiated smoothing impacted billed amounts. This ticket consolidates requirement, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for the unified mapping and invoice presentation.
scope: In scope: mapping rules engine, meter transformation (tokens -> normalized compute units), console invoice UI sections, reconciliation checks, acceptance tests, and rollout gating. Out of scope: core runtime changes to how Dedicated charges compute credits at kernel level (handled by ENG follow-up), third-party accounting exports format changes (separate follow-up).
goals: 1) Single canonical ledger entries for hybrid customers that can be reconciled to both hosted token streams and dedicated compute credit consumption. 2) Console invoice/views that present a human-readable breakdown: baseline committed usage, burst usage, smoothing/fallback adjustments, and per-route model-level surcharge. 3) Billing acceptance criteria satisfied with automated reconciliation coverage for top 95% of customers by spend.
tradeoffs_and_considerations:
- Option A: Convert hosted tokens to a normalized compute unit using model and seq-length profiles (more accurate per-call reconciliation, higher engineering cost).
- Option B: Maintain separate ledgers but present a combined view in the console (lower backend changes but hard to support negotiated smoothing).
Decision: implement Option A for correctness for enterprise rollout; provide a backward-compatible display mode for existing self-serve customers.
implementation_notes: - Build a transformation service that consumes hosted token streams and emits normalized compute-units (NCU) keyed by customer_id + model_variant + route. - Reuse existing compute-credit ledger schema but add source_type enum (hosted|dedicated|adjustment). - Capture burst/spillover flags at request-time and tag ledger entries with smoothing_window_id when enterprise smoothing is applied. - Ensure idempotent ingest to ledger and deterministic mapping to avoid double-billing on retries.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Reconciliation: For a set of 20 synthetic hybrid accounts (mix of hosted calls and dedicated jobs), daily ledger totals match a ground-truth simulator within 0.5% for 95% of accounts and within 1.5% for all.
2) Invoice presentation: Console invoice shows 'Hybrid total', with collapsible rows: Committed Dedicated, Hosted bursts (NCU), Smoothing adjustments, Net Charged. Stakeholder signoff from Billing PM and Finance required.
3) Edge-case behavior: If a request is retried and both hosted and dedicated lines appear, the ledger deduplicates to the first-processed idempotency_key.
4) Rate-limits & quotas: Per-route quota checks continue to enforce separate runtime SLOs; billing mapping must not change runtime denial semantics.
5) Acceptance tests: End-to-end tests simulate overage, refund and negotiated smoothing; automated tests pass in CI and results displayed on the billing dashboard.
6) Metrics: New metrics emitted: ncu_emitted_total, ncu_mapped_hosted_total, smoothing_adjustments_total; alerts configured for >0.5% daily discrepancy across aggregate ledger vs. invoice export.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for conversion logic with model profiles and sequence-length weighting. 2) Integration tests: inject hosted token events and dedicated job events, validate ledger entries and final invoice generator. 3) Load test: 10k hybrid events/sec to ensure transformation service scales. 4) Manual QA: Finance-run reconciliation workbook comparing old invoices vs. new hybrid presentation for three pilot customers. 5) Production canary: route 5% of enterprise hybrid traffic through mapping service with shadow billing and reconciliation checks for 7 days.
qa_and_release_gating:
- QA signoff required from Billing PM, Finance Ops, and a Solutions Engineer for each pilot customer.
- Data migration/backfill plan: run one-time mapper against 90 days of historical hosted tokens for pilot accounts; verify ledger idempotency.
- Blocker criteria: any unexplained >1% net discrepancy on pilot customer invoices or inability to attribute >95% of billable events to a ledger entry.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal pilot with three enterprise customers (canary) using shadow mode (no invoice change). Phase 2: Offer opt-in unified invoices for selected customers with pricing addendum. Phase 3: Global default for new accounts and automated migration tool for legacy accounts. Each phase includes two-week observation windows and rollback playbooks.
monitoring_and_alerts: Emit reconciliation drift metric and set SLO: <0.5% daily drift. Configure alert to Billing on-call when drift >0.5% for 3 consecutive hours. Create Grafana dashboard with per-customer drift, NCU issuance rates, smoothing_adjustments per day.
open_questions: 1) What is canonical conversion factor for newer quantized models without historical seq-length profiles? Proposed: use median sequence length from last 14 days as fallback. 2) How to present negotiated smoothing in invoices without exposing internal discounts? Proposed: show a line 'Smoothing adjustment (negotiated)'. 3) Do we need legal approval for modifying invoice structure for active contracts? Action: Legal consult requested (linked).
next_steps: 1) ENG: spike on conversion accuracy and ingest idempotency (owner: eng-owner-queue). 2) Finance: prepare reconciliation workbook and pilot customer list. 3) PM: schedule Legal review and Solutions Engineer customer readiness checks. 4) Design: finalize invoice panel microcopy. Target next sync: 2026-03-18.
